transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, mostly I came in because I’m tired in a way that just doesn’t really make sense. I mean, I can sleep fine, and I'm keeping up with everything at work, but I still feel like I’m running on a low battery before the day even gets going.
Do you find that you have lost interest or pleasure in the things you usually enjoy doing?

Yeah, I suppose I have. It's... well, for a long time now, there's just been this gray, flat feeling on most days. 

Even the things I used to really look forward to—like taking the boat out fishing, tending to my tomatoes, or going to a church concert—they don't really do much for me anymore. They just feel like items on a checklist, you know? Just another thing to get through instead of something I actually enjoy.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been quite a while. I guess... well, this has really been going on since I was pulled back into full operational leadership at work. That was about two years and four months ago, I'd say.
During these past two years, have there been any periods where your mood felt significantly worse than your current 'gray, flat' baseline, or has it been consistently the same level of low?

No, I wouldn't say it's ever gotten significantly worse than that. It's really just been... pretty consistent. Just that same flat, low level the whole time. I haven't had any major crashes or anything like that, just this steady lack of energy and interest day in and day out.
Have you noticed any physical changes, such as feeling unusually cold even when others are comfortable, or perhaps changes in the texture of your skin or hair?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't feel colder than usual, and my skin and hair seem about the same as they always have. It's really just the mood and the energy that's been off.
During these past two years, have you found it difficult to concentrate or make decisions?

No, I haven't really had any trouble with that. I mean, I'm still running operations at work, so I have to make decisions every day. My concentration seems fine. It's not a focus issue... it's really just that flat feeling and the lack of energy I mentioned. But my mind is still sharp enough.
How would you describe your general sense of self-esteem or how you feel about yourself during these past two years?

My self-esteem? I'd say it's... it's fine, really. I don't feel bad about myself or anything like that. I mean, I know I'm good at my job, and I've been doing it a long time. I don't feel worthless or like a failure. It's just... it's just that lack of joy or energy I was talking about. But as far as how I view myself, that hasn't really changed.
